text:
Jess (Acme): Hey — after rotating our API key yesterday every request to /v1/chat/completions returns 401 invalid_api_key. We rolled the key via the dashboard and updated our CI; still failing.

Maya (Support): Sorry about that — can you paste the exact curl you ran (sanitized) and whether this is hosted or dedicated?

Jess (Acme): Hosted. Here's the sanitized curl we used:

```
curl -i -H \"Authorization: Api-Key xQw9R7m...t2V^\" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat/completions -d '{"model":"rdr-small","input":"hi"}'
```

Maya (Support): Hmm I see a `^` at the end of the key in that header. Did you copy the key from a Windows machine or a terminal that might insert/control characters?

Jess (Acme): We did copy it from a Windows devbox. We thought caret was part of the key (copied by mistake). The key in dashboard doesn't show it. Not sure how it got appended.

Jon (Eng): Small theory — Windows cmd.exe will use `^` as an escape character for newlines and some paste tools insert it when copying multiline values. If a trailing `^` got added it changes the key bytes and causes a 401. Can you run this and paste the hex of the header value?

Jess (Acme): Ran `printf` on WSL, here's the visible header we send now: `Authorization: Api-Key xQw9R7m...t2V^`

Maya (Support): Please try copying the key again from the dashboard into a simple text editor (not Powershell/cmd) and then curl with the header in quotes. Also try the SDK with the exact key string.

Jess (Acme): Re-copied into Notepad and re-ran, success — the same request returns 200 now. Looks like the caret was the culprit.

Jon (Eng): For root cause, check any automation that manipulates the key string: CI scripts, config templates, or a wrapper that might add an escape. Windows paste helpers or some CLI prompt utilities append `^` when joining lines. If you need, we can escalate to a quick remote debug session.

Maya (Support): Glad that fixed it. I'll leave a short repro & mitigation here:
- Repro: copy API key from dashboard on Windows, paste into cmd.exe where caret may appear when pasting multi-line or wrapped text. Use `curl -H \"Authorization: Api-Key <key>\"` and observe 401.
- Mitigation: paste into a plain editor (Notepad), remove any trailing control characters (caret, BOM, invisible chars), then re-copy. Enclose the key in quotes in shells where whitespace/escapes are meaningful.

Jess (Acme): Thanks — we patched our internal README to say: copy from dashboard -> Notepad -> CI secret store.

deploy-bot: rotational-key event: rotated key id K-9x7 at 2024-08-21T14:02:00Z (for audit).

Maya (Support): I'll close after 48h if no recurrence. Feel free to reopen with logs/hex if it happens again. :thumbsup:
